subject: Clarify ambiguous SIG entries: key custody vs backup sovereignty — Ridgeview
messages:
From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@ridgeview.com>

Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@ridgeview.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG Q: key custody vs backup/residency (need clarification)

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for working with us on the SIG. We hit an ambiguity in two related questions and wanted a short written clarification before we mark the answers in our portal:

- Q: "Does your organization retain the ability to access customer encryption keys used to protect backups?" — The SIG wording could mean "does Redwood retain keys for backups you manage on behalf of customers" or "does Redwood have the operational ability to decrypt customer-managed backups if asked by the customer."

- Q: "Are backups stored in a location that may result in residency differences from customer data?" — the follow-up: does this refer to snapshot copies created for service maintenance vs. customer-initiated exports?

Can we get a quick written interpretation (bullet form) and any evidence artifacts you can attach? If helpful, happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow.

Best,
Asha
Security Operations
Ridgeview Capital

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@ridgeview.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@ridgeview.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG Q: key custody vs backup/residency (need clarification)

Hi Asha,

Thanks — good questions. Short answers up front, then proposed next steps:

1) Key custody for backups: Redwood does NOT retain customer encryption keys when a customer elects customer-managed keys (CMK) for backups. If a customer uses Redwood-managed keys (default), Redwood does hold the key material in our KMS and will perform backup encryption/decryption as part of normal service operations.

2) Backup residency: Backups created by standard service operations (automated snapshots for replication/maintenance) are stored according to the deployment's region/policy. We do not copy snapshots to different legal jurisdictions except when customer explicitly requests cross-region replication or when using our Dedicated/Private offering with multi-region replication enabled. Exports initiated by customers (download/export) are treated as customer data and follow the destination the customer chooses.

Next steps:
- I can send a concise two-paragraph written interpretation for you to upload to the SIG portal.
- We can attach a short evidence bundle (KMS configuration diagram + excerpt of our backup retention policy).
- If agreeable, propose a 20-min call today (3pm PT) to confirm and capture any wording Ridgeview prefers.

I'll draft the written text now and follow up with attachments.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

Adding one detail for the record: when a customer uses CMK and later requests a restore, the restore operation must be authorized using the customer's key; Redwood cannot decrypt without that key material or an API token scoped by the customer. We'll include a one-page KMS flow diagram in the evidence pdf.

Irene

Subject: Notes and decisions from 2026-11-19 call (SIG clarifications)

Attendees: Marcus Lin (Redwood), Irene Choi (Redwood), Mina Haddad (Redwood), Asha Patel (Ridgeview), Oliver Grant (Ridgeview), Samuel "Sam" Torres (Ridgeview infra)

Summary / agreed interpretations (for SIG portal):
- Q: Key custody for backups: agreed text: "If a customer configures customer-managed keys (CMK), Redwood does not retain or have operational access to those key materials for decrypting backups. If a customer uses Redwood-managed keys, Redwood stores and uses key material in our KMS to perform backup encryption/decryption as part of routine operations."
- Q: Backup residency: agreed text: "Backups generated by automated service processes are stored in the same region as the customer deployment by default. Cross-region replication or storage in a different legal jurisdiction is only performed when explicitly requested by the customer or enabled via a documented replication feature (customer opt-in). Customer-initiated exports follow the destination chosen by the customer at export time."
- Emergency access: we confirmed there is no policy that routinely moves key material across jurisdictions for emergency access. Any emergency procedure requires documented approvals and will be logged; details of sensitive operations can be reviewed during SOC2/third-party audits.

Action items:
- Redwood: attach evidence bundle (KMS flow diagram + backup storage excerpt) and written interpretation for SIG portal (Marcus) — target EOD Thu 11/19.
- Ridgeview: confirm final wording in portal and let us know if they need additional artifacts.

Attachment stubs shared in call: redwood-kms-evidence-summary.pdf; ridgeview-sig-annotated-answers.docx

Notes: call recorded (for internal note-taking only); we kept the language intentionally conservative for audit review.

Marcus
